notes: Portable AgentKit template. scripts/run_mcp_builder_live_benchmark.py replaces __AGENTKIT_WORKSPACE__ with an absolute path before execution.
Scenarios intentionally cover build, review/security, and boundary behavior.
This benchmark performs real codex exec runs.
setupQuestions: Can MCP Builder turn a small REST API into a capability-first MCP design and implementation?
Does MCP Builder keep review and remediation distinct unless fixes are requested?
Does MCP Builder identify security boundaries without inventing execution evidence?
Does MCP Builder narrow scope when a request belongs to another plugin?

scenarios.title: Build a capability-first customer support MCP server
scenarios.purpose: Measure the flagship create-mcp-server workflow on a realistic API fixture.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "mcp-builder". Inspect openapi.yaml and README.md. Design and implement a small Python MCP server for the customer-support API. Model business capabilities instead of mirroring endpoints. The minimum useful surface is customer.search, customer.get, customer.notes.append, ticket.search, and ticket.get. Add focused tests for valid, invalid, empty-result and backend-failure behavior. Do not claim tests passed unless you actually execute them.
successChecklist: A real MCP server implementation is created on disk.
The capability surface is task-oriented rather than endpoint-oriented.
The five required customer/ticket capabilities are represented.
Tests cover positive and negative/failure paths.
The final answer distinguishes generated work from executed validation.

scenarios.title: Review and secure an existing MCP server without premature remediation
scenarios.purpose: Measure review routing, severity, security reasoning and review-before-fix behavior.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "mcp-builder". Review starter_server.py as an existing MCP-style server. Do not modify it. Produce an evidence-backed review covering capability design, agent usability, authentication/authorization, tenant isolation, secret handling, destructive/write operations, error handling and tests. Classify findings by severity and clearly separate observed evidence from inferred risk.
successChecklist: The review includes capability, reliability and MCP-specific security findings.
The run does not claim tests or security validation were executed when they were not.

scenarios.title: Respect the plugin boundary on a .NET-only request
scenarios.purpose: Check that MCP Builder does not force itself onto an unrelated .NET code-quality task.
scenarios.userInput: This workspace also contains SampleService.cs. The request is only to review ordinary .NET naming and async practices; there is no MCP code involved. Use the local Codex plugin "mcp-builder" only if it actually applies. Do not edit files. Explain the appropriate boundary and leave unrelated work alone.
successChecklist: The response recognizes that ordinary .NET review is outside MCP Builder's core responsibility.
The plugin does not invent an MCP angle to justify itself.
